S42.01.needs: A paid account (Scheduled tasks are available on Basic and higher plans). A Free account may see the page locked.
S42.01.note: Delivery is shown on the Scheduled page and by the Scheduled task finished notification (see S42.17); the in-app delivery path was not traced end to end.
steps: Sign in and click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Click the arrow button beside New task, then click Start from a template.
Click the card named Daily briefing (it shows Weekdays at 8:00 AM).
Submit the Create Schedule dialog (the submit button's exact text was not checked).
Look for the new schedule card named Daily briefing with a Next: row of upcoming times, and compare with Expected (recurring, generated and delivered).
S42.01.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > (arrow button beside it) > Start from a template > Daily briefing

S42.04.note: The ScheduleForm line cited in Code moved; the Local Time and Time Zone fields are at lines 387 and 510 today.
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar, then New task.
Click Create from scratch (or start from a template).
Set Recurrence, then change Local Time.
Change Time Zone (the field offers a list of zones).
Save, then look at the card's Next: row, whose tooltip reads Times are shown in <zone>, and compare with Expected.
S42.04.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > New task > Create from scratch > Local Time and Time Zone fields

S42.15.needs: A paid account with at least one schedule.
S42.15.note: The switch has no visible text; it is labelled only by its aria-label Pause <name> or Resume <name>.
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
Find the Daily briefing card.
Click its switch to pause it; look for the Paused text on the card and the message Schedule paused.
Click the switch again; look for Schedule resumed and the card's Paused text going away, and compare with Expected.
S42.15.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the briefing's card > its on/off switch (labelled Pause or Resume by name)

S42.16.needs: A way to see push notifications (a phone with AGI installed) for the hold to be checked. Web alone only shows the Quiet hours are active banner.
S42.16.note: Approvals and failures are exempt from the hold, as the page text says. The push hold lives in apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts (heldByQuietHours); its cited line moved.
steps: Open the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar and click Settings.
Click Time and focus.
Turn on Quiet hours and set a start and an end time that differ.
Keep the page open during those hours (or set a window that includes now) and look for the banner Quiet hours are active.
Holding of push notifications happens on the server; check on a phone with push that a non-exempt notification is held, and compare with Expected.
S42.16.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours

S42.17.needs: An email inbox and/or a phone with AGI push, plus a scheduled task that can run.
S42.17.note: Earlier check only saw the channels; delivery was not tested. The web settings row offers Email and Mobile push, not a browser channel, for this event.
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings, then Notifications.
Find the row Scheduled task finished with its channel switches (Email, Mobile push).
Turn the channels on or off and note the change.
Run a scheduled task and wait for it to finish, then check the email or phone push for the finished or failed message.
Compare what arrives with Expected.
S42.17.where: Account menu > Settings > Notifications > Scheduled task finished

labels.text: Turn on Memory and Save memories from chats to create a recap.

S42.19.needs: Memory and Save memories from chats turned on, and a paid or signed-in account with past chats. Without them the page is blocked.
S42.19.note: The earlier check named Generate from past chats, but the code's visible text says Save memories from chats. Memory is the gate, as the earlier check found.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Reflect.
Read the page. If it says Turn on Memory and Save memories from chats to create a recap, turn those two settings on under Personalization and reload.
Choose a range in the Reflect range dropdown (Past 30 days by default).
Look for the usage reflection (topics and times) and compare with Expected.

S42.21.needs: Memory and Save memories from chats turned on, with a year of chats.
S42.21.note: No screen says Annual recap. The recap is the Past year range of the Reflect page, not a calendar-year report. Gated the same way as S42.19.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Reflect.
Open the Reflect range dropdown and choose Past year.
Wait for the recap to reload.
Look at the recap for the last 365 days and compare with Expected (a recap of the past year).
S42.21.where: Account menu > Settings > Reflect > Reflect range > Past year

S42.22.needs: Patience: the reminder needs the chosen amount of visible time in AGI that day.
S42.22.note: The reminder is shown once a day, per the page text (one gentle nudge each day). The minimum option length was not checked.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Time and focus.
Set Break reminder to the shortest value offered.
Go back to a chat and keep using AGI in the same tab until the chosen time has passed.
Look for the box Time for a break? and compare with Expected.
S42.22.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus > Break reminder

S42.23.note: The nav label Time and focus comes from packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/settings.json (key time-focus).
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings.
Click Time and focus in the settings list.
Look for the sections Break reminder and Quiet hours on the page.
Change one of them, look for the save status line, and compare with Expected.
S42.23.where: Account menu > Settings > Time and focus

S42.25.needs: A schedule that has run at least once.
S42.25.note: No visible text says saved editions. Recent results (RecentScheduleResults.tsx) is also a history list, but its visible heading was not found in the code.
steps: Click Scheduled in the sidebar.
On the Daily briefing card, click the History icon (title Run History).
Look at the list of past runs with their status (for example completed, failed, timeout).
Open a run to see its result, and compare with Expected (past briefings kept as a browsable history).
S42.25.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > the briefing's card > History icon (title Run History)
